segments.speaker: Dana
segments.text: Yeah, so quick pipeline check. Hartley Manufacturing and Ridgeview Clinics are the two that can still close for February if we get the last pieces in.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Okay. Hartley first. That's the 57 seats, right, $46,800 annual?

segments.speaker: Dana
segments.text: Right. Procurement is good with 57 seats, annual upfront, February 28 start. The only thing holding it is their auto-renewal redline. I’ve nudged legal every morning since last Wednesday, and again yesterday afternoon, for the answer or sign-off. The customer is ready, but the deal is stalled until legal sends that back.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Got it. If they approve the redline today, can Hartley sign today?

segments.speaker: Dana
segments.text: Yes. Their director already said she can sign by 4 p.m. Central if the terms are final. No pricing issue, no seat issue.

segments.speaker: Dana
segments.text: Ridgeview is 32 seats at $29,400, with a March 11 go-live. They asked whether we can include the basic onboarding package without changing the subscription line. I keep nudging services for that sign-off, twice Monday and once this morning, because the order form is sitting there and the deal is stalled until services confirms it.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Understood. Do they need anything else from us besides that onboarding confirmation?

segments.speaker: Dana
segments.text: No, the invoice timing is fine, net 30 is fine, and they accepted the 12-month term. Their CFO just doesn't want a surprise services line showing up later.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Okay. Keep the customer warm on both, but don't change the numbers. If either approval comes in, send me the final language before it goes out.
